name: Gompertz–Makeham Force of Mortality
description: Gives the instantaneous death rate at age x: an age-independent part A plus a Gompertz part that grows exponentially with age.
notes: The default parameters are those of the Standard Ultimate Life Table used in actuarial exams (A = 0.00022, B = 2.7 × 10⁻⁶, c = 1.124 there).

name: Makeham Survival Probability ₜpₓ
description: Gives the probability that a life aged x survives t more years under Gompertz–Makeham mortality.
notes: With the Standard Ultimate Life Table parameters a 60-year-old survives ten years with probability about 0.9147.

name: De Moivre Survival Probability
description: Gives ₜpₓ when deaths are spread uniformly up to a limiting age ω (de Moivre 1725).
notes: A simple teaching model; real mortality rises with age.

name: Probability of Surviving Several Years (from qₓ List)
description: Multiplies the yearly survival probabilities 1 − qₓ to get the chance of surviving all the years in the list.
notes: Here about 0.7676 for ten years.

name: Curtate Life Expectancy over the Table
expression: sum(k, 1, len(q), prod(j, 1, k, 1 - at(q, j)))
description: Adds the probabilities of surviving 1, 2, … whole years: the expected number of complete years lived within the table.
notes: Add about 0.5 for the complete expectation of life (deaths spread evenly within years).

name: Whole Life Insurance APV (Constant Force)
description: Gives the actuarial present value of 1 paid at the moment of death when mortality and interest are both constant: μ/(μ + δ).
notes: A classic closed form; about 0.2857 here.

name: Term Insurance APV (Constant Force)
description: Gives the present value of 1 paid at death if it happens within n years, under constant forces.
notes: Tends to the whole-life value as n grows.

name: Pure Endowment APV (Constant Force)
description: Gives the present value of 1 paid at time n only if the insured is still alive then: ₙEₓ = ₙpₓ vⁿ.
notes: Term insurance plus pure endowment gives endowment insurance.

name: Continuous Life Annuity APV (Constant Force)
description: Gives the present value of 1 a year paid continuously while alive, for at most n years, under constant forces.
notes: For whole life (n → ∞) it is 1/(μ + δ). Note Ā = 1 − δ·ā always holds.

name: Discrete Whole-Table Insurance APV (from qₓ List)
expression: sum(k, 1, len(q), prod(j, 1, k - 1, 1 - at(q, j)) * at(q, k) / (1 + i_r)^k)
description: Gives the present value of 1 paid at the end of the year of death within the years covered by the list (a term insurance): Σ ₖpₓ qₓ₊ₖ v^(k+1).
notes: Extend the list to the end of the life table for a whole-life value.

name: Life Annuity-Due APV (from qₓ List)
expression: sum(k, 0, len(q) - 1, prod(j, 1, k, 1 - at(q, j)) / (1 + i_r)^k)
description: Gives the present value of 1 paid at the start of each year while alive, over the years in the list (a temporary annuity-due).
notes: Premiums payable yearly in advance are valued with this factor.

name: Net Annual Premium (Equivalence Principle)
expression: sa * sum(k, 1, len(q), prod(j, 1, k - 1, 1 - at(q, j)) * at(q, k) / (1 + i_r)^k) / sum(k, 0, len(q) - 1, prod(j, 1, k, 1 - at(q, j)) / (1 + i_r)^k)
description: Gives the level yearly premium, paid in advance while alive, for term insurance over the years in the list: premium income and benefit outgo have equal present value.
notes: Add loadings for expenses and profit to reach the office (gross) premium.

name: Mortality Improvement Projection
description: Projects a death rate forward assuming it falls by a fixed percentage each year.
notes: Pension schemes use improvement scales like this (e.g. CMI, MP-2021).

name: Lee–Carter Death Rate
description: Gives the central death rate from the Lee–Carter model ln mₓ,ₜ = aₓ + bₓkₜ, widely used to forecast mortality.
notes: kₜ usually falls over time and is forecast as a random walk with drift.

name: Joint-Life Survival (Independent Lives)
description: Gives the probability that both of two independent lives survive the period.
notes: Used for joint-life annuities that stop at the first death.

name: Last-Survivor Survival
description: Gives the probability that at least one of two independent lives survives.
notes: Survivor pensions for couples are valued with this.

name: Monthly Death Probability from Annual (Constant Force)
description: Converts an annual death (or lapse, or default) probability to a monthly one assuming a constant force within the year.
notes: Dividing by 12 is a close but slightly higher approximation.

name: Loss Ratio
description: Divides incurred claims (including loss adjustment expenses if desired) by earned premium.
notes: The core profitability measure of an insurance portfolio.

name: Combined Ratio
description: Adds the loss ratio and the expense ratio. Below 100 % means an underwriting profit.
notes: Investment income can still make an insurer profitable above 100 %.

name: Pure Premium (Frequency × Severity)
description: Gives the expected claim cost per unit of exposure: claim frequency times average severity.
notes: The starting point of ratemaking before expense and profit loadings.

name: Gross Premium with Expense and Profit Loadings
description: Loads a pure premium for fixed and variable expenses and a profit margin (the standard indicated-rate formula).
notes: Here the gross premium is 500.

name: Expected-Value Premium Principle
description: Charges the expected loss plus a proportional safety loading θ.
notes: Simple, but it ignores how variable the risk is.

name: Standard-Deviation Premium Principle
description: Charges the expected loss plus a multiple of its standard deviation, so riskier contracts cost more.
notes: Variance principle: replace sd by the variance and use a much smaller α.

name: Exponential Premium Principle (Exponential Claims)
description: Gives the premium (1/a) ln E[e^(aX)] from exponential utility, for an exponentially distributed claim with mean θ.
notes: Requires aθ < 1. As a → 0 it tends to the mean θ.

name: Full Credibility Standard (Claim Count)
description: Gives the number of claims needed for full credibility in limited-fluctuation credibility: the observed frequency is within ±k of the truth with probability p.
notes: The classic standard with p = 90 % and k = 5 % is about 1082 claims.

name: Partial Credibility Factor (Square-Root Rule)
description: Gives the credibility weight Z = √(n/n_full), capped at 1.
notes: The estimate is then Z × (own experience) + (1 − Z) × (prior or class rate).

name: Bühlmann Credibility Factor
description: Gives the Bühlmann credibility Z = n/(n + k) with k = EPV/VHM.
notes: The more the risks differ from each other (high VHM), the more weight own experience gets.

name: Credibility-Weighted Estimate
description: Blends own experience and the collective estimate with credibility weight Z.
notes: The basis of experience rating and bonus–malus systems.

name: Compound Poisson Aggregate Claims Variance
description: Gives the variance of total claims when the claim count is Poisson: λ E[X²].
notes: The mean is λ E[X]. The coefficient of variation shrinks like 1/√λ as the portfolio grows.

name: Ruin Probability (Cramér–Lundberg, Exponential Claims)
description: Gives the probability that an insurer's surplus ever falls below zero in the classical compound-Poisson model with exponential claims.
notes: Grows smaller exponentially as the starting capital increases.

name: Adjustment Coefficient (Exponential Claims)
description: Gives the Lundberg adjustment coefficient R, which sets the rate at which ruin probability falls with capital: ψ(u) ≤ e^(−Ru).
notes: Solves 1 + (1 + θ)E[X]R = M_X(R); for exponential claims it has this closed form.

name: Expected Payment per Loss with a Deductible (Exponential Severity)
description: Gives the insurer's expected payment per loss, E[(X − d)₊], for exponentially distributed losses.
notes: Equals the stop-loss premium with retention d.

name: Loss Elimination Ratio (Exponential Severity)
description: Gives the share of expected losses removed by a deductible d: E[X ∧ d]/E[X].
notes: A 250 deductible removes about 22 % of expected losses when the mean loss is 1000.

name: Limited Expected Value (Pareto Severity)
description: Gives E[X ∧ u] for a Pareto (Lomax) loss, the expected payment under a policy limit u.
notes: Pareto losses have heavy tails, so limits matter much more than for exponential losses.

name: Excess-of-Loss Reinsurance Recovery
description: Gives what a reinsurer pays on one loss for the layer "limit xs retention".
notes: Here the 2m xs 1m layer pays its full 2,000,000.

name: Unearned Premium Reserve (Pro Rata)
description: Gives the part of a premium not yet earned at the valuation date, spread evenly over the policy term.
notes: The liability for cover still to be provided.

name: Chain-Ladder Development Factor
description: Gives the volume-weighted age-to-age factor used in chain-ladder reserving: total claims at the next age over total at this age.
notes: Only accident years with both ages observed belong in the lists.

name: Chain-Ladder Ultimate Claims
description: Projects a year's claims to their ultimate value by multiplying the latest total by the remaining development factors.
notes: Subtract the reported claims to get the IBNR reserve.

name: Bornhuetter–Ferguson Reserve
description: Estimates unreported claims as the expected losses times the share still to develop, 1 − 1/CDF (Bornhuetter–Ferguson 1972).
notes: Steadier than the chain ladder for recent years with little data.

name: Solvency Capital Aggregation (Two Risks)
description: Combines two capital requirements with a correlation, as in the Solvency II standard formula.
notes: Correlation below 1 gives a diversification benefit: 127.3 here instead of 160.

name: Solvency Ratio
description: Divides available capital by the required capital; regulators require at least 100 %.
notes: Many insurers target 150–200 %.

name: Premium for a Level Term Policy (Constant Force, Continuous)
description: With constant mortality and interest the level premium rate of any term or whole-life policy paid continuously is simply μ per unit of cover.
notes: The interest rate drops out: each instant's premium exactly pays that instant's expected claims.

name: Probability of at Least One Claim (Poisson)
description: Gives the chance of one or more claims in a period when the number of claims is Poisson.
notes: For small λ it is close to λ itself.

name: Bonus–Malus Premium after k Claim-Free Years
description: Applies a simple linear no-claims discount down to a floor.
notes: Real systems use step tables and move back up after a claim.
